joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.question: In John 1:14, the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.
joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.feedbackCorrect: John states that the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 1:14: the Word became flesh and dwelt among us.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.hint: Read the beginning of the verse.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.question: In John 1:14, tap the name John gives Jesus in this chapter.
joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.feedbackCorrect: John calls Jesus the Word who became flesh among us.

feedbackWrong.a: "graça" describes what he is like, not his name.
feedbackWrong.b: "carne" is what the Word became, not his name.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.hint: Look for the name at the start of the verse.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.question: According to John 1:12, what do those who believe in Jesus' name receive?
joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.feedbackCorrect: Whoever receives Jesus and believes in his name receives power to be God's child.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of becoming God's children, not of judging.
feedbackWrong.b: The gift is sonship with God, not a position of honor.
feedbackWrong.c: The new birth comes from God, not from a lineage.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.hint: See what God gives to those who receive him.

options.a: The right to judge others
options.b: A position among the leaders
options.c: The name of a human family
options.d: The power to become children of God

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.question: Arrange John 1:14 in the order of the text.
joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.feedbackCorrect: The Word becomes flesh, full of grace and truth, and his glory is seen.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the Word becoming flesh; the glory seen closes the verse.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.hint: The verse begins with the Word.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.question: In John 1:11, what did his own not do with Jesus?
joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus came to what was his own, but his own did not receive him.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of not receiving Jesus, not merely hearing.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of not receiving Jesus when he came.

joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.question: What does John 1:14 convey that connects to this context?
joao-sem-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.feedbackCorrect: The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, present in human life.

feedbackWrong.b: The focus here is the Word present, not the law alone.
feedbackWrong.c: The text shows God present among us, not distant.

options.a: The Word became flesh
options.b: The law is enough by itself
options.c: God withdraws from humans

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.question: In John 1:11–12, all who were Jesus' own received him without exception.
joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says his own did not receive him; only those who receive him are children.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread John 1:11: his own did not receive him when he came.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.question: In John 1:12, tap the word that marks the contrast with the earlier rejection.
joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.feedbackCorrect: After the rejection, the text turns the page to those who receive him.

feedbackWrong.a: "nome" says in whom they believe; the contrast is at the start.
feedbackWrong.c: "todos" says how many receive; the contrast is in the first word.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.hint: It is the first word of the verse.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.question: How does John 1:12 relate to John 1:11?
joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.feedbackCorrect: Beside the rejection, the text shows who receives Jesus as God's child.

feedbackWrong.a: Birth as God's child comes from God, in 1:13.
feedbackWrong.b: God's child is one who receives Jesus, not one who rejects him.
feedbackWrong.c: The text ties sonship to receiving Jesus and believing in him.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.hint: Think about the contrast between the two verses.

options.a: Human birth guarantees faith
options.b: Whoever rejects Jesus becomes his child
options.c: Believing is unnecessary to be a child
options.d: Whoever receives Jesus becomes God's child

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.question: How does the scene in John 1:11–12 move forward?
joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.feedbackCorrect: First rejection, then the welcome of those who believe and become children.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the coming without welcome; becoming children is the result.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.hint: The result of believing comes last.

options.a: Jesus comes and is not received
options.b: Those who receive him believe in his name
options.c: They become children of God

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.question: In John 1:16, where does the grace upon grace that all received come from?
joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.feedbackCorrect: All received from Jesus' fullness, grace upon grace without measure.

feedbackWrong.b: Glory is seen in 1:14; here all receive from his full source.
feedbackWrong.c: Truth appears in 1:14 and 1:17; here the source is another word.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.hint: Look for the word tied to receiving.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.question: What links John 1:12 to John 20:31?
joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, believing in Jesus is at the center of John's message.

feedbackWrong.b: Rejecting is the opposite of the believing both texts highlight.
feedbackWrong.c: John 1:13 denies that sonship comes from human lineage.

joao-cam-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.hint: See the goal John gives his book.

options.a: Believing in Jesus' name
options.b: Rejecting the Word who was sent
options.c: Being born of human lineage

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.question: In John 1:13, being a child of God does not depend on human will.
joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.feedbackCorrect: Birth as God's child comes from God, not from human will.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 1:13: not of the will of man, but of God.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-01.hint: See where this birth comes from.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.question: In John 1:14, tap the phrase that shows Jesus becoming human.
joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.feedbackCorrect: The Word became flesh, becoming human without ceasing to be who he is.

feedbackWrong.a: Dwelling among us tells where he lived; becoming human comes first.
feedbackWrong.b: Full of grace describes what he is like; becoming human comes first.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-02.hint: Look for the verb about becoming.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.question: What reading does John 1:13–14 support about Jesus?
joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-03.feedbackCorrect: The Word who was with God became flesh and dwelt among us.

feedbackWrong.a: John 1:13 says this birth comes from God.
feedbackWrong.b: An idea does not become flesh or dwell among people.
feedbackWrong.c: The text shows his glory as of the only begotten of the Father.

options.a: Being a child of God comes by lineage
options.b: The Word is just an abstract idea
options.c: Jesus is only an ordinary human teacher

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the Word in the Bible's story?
joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.feedbackCorrect: From creation to the Word made flesh, to life given to those who believe.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story, from creation in Genesis to life in John 20:31.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-04.hint: Follow the order, from Genesis to the end of John.

options.a: In the beginning, God creates heaven and earth
options.b: The Word becomes flesh among us
options.c: Whoever believes has life in his name

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.question: In John 1:17, what came through Jesus Christ together with truth?
joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.feedbackCorrect: Grace and truth came together through Jesus Christ.

feedbackWrong.a: Life is a theme in John, but here truth is paired with another word.
feedbackWrong.b: Glory is seen in 1:14; here truth is paired with another word.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-05.hint: It is the word that comes before truth.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.question: What links John 1:14 to Genesis 1:1?
joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.feedbackCorrect: The Word who became flesh was already with God at the beginning of all.

feedbackWrong.a: The Word already existed before becoming flesh in John 1:14.
feedbackWrong.c: Genesis begins with God creating; matter is not eternal.

joao-pro-jo-01-verbo-sinais-06.hint: See who is already present in the beginning.

options.a: Jesus begins only at his birth
options.b: God present from the beginning
options.c: Matter has always existed

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-01.question: In John 14:6, Jesus says that Thomas is the way, the truth and the life.
joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-01.feedbackCorrect: The one who claims to be the way, the truth and the life is Jesus himself.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread John 14:6: it is Jesus who says he is the way.

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-01.hint: See who is speaking and about whom.

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-02.question: In John 14:6, tap the first word Jesus uses to present himself.
joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus presents himself first as the way to the Father.

feedbackWrong.a: "vida" is the third word; the first comes right after "Eu sou".
feedbackWrong.b: "verdade" is the second word; the first comes right after "Eu sou".

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-03.question: According to John 14:8, what does Philip ask Jesus?
joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-03.feedbackCorrect: Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father, and says that is enough.

feedbackWrong.a: Philip does not ask for a delay; he asks to see the Father.
feedbackWrong.c: Philip does not ask for an explanation; he asks to see the Father.
feedbackWrong.d: Philip's request is to see the Father, not to go to the temple.

options.a: To delay his departure
options.b: To show them the Father
options.c: To explain a hard parable
options.d: To take them to the temple

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-04.question: Arrange John 14:6 in the order of the text.
joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-04.feedbackCorrect: Jesus presents himself as way, truth and life, and points to the Father.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who is speaking; reaching the Father closes the verse.

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-04.hint: The verse begins with who is speaking.

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-05.question: In John 14:3, what will Jesus prepare for the disciples?
joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus will prepare a place and will return to receive his own.

feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of preparing a place and coming back for them.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of preparing a place for the disciples.

joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-06.question: What does John 14:6 convey that connects to this context?
joao-sem-jo-02-eu-sou-06.feedbackCorrect: Before leaving, Jesus shows that he himself is the way to the Father.

feedbackWrong.a: Whoever sees Jesus sees the Father; he is not far from God.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus says no one comes to the Father except through him.

options.a: The Father is far from Jesus
options.b: Many ways lead to the Father
options.c: Jesus is the way to the Father

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-01.question: In John 14:5–6, Thomas already knows where Jesus is going and asks nothing.
joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-01.feedbackCorrect: Thomas admits he does not know the way, and Jesus answers him.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread John 14:5: Thomas says he does not know where Jesus is going.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-02.question: In John 14:9, tap the phrase that shows Jesus' long time with them.
joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus reminds them he has been with the disciples for so long.

feedbackWrong.a: Philip is the one asking; the time together comes after.
feedbackWrong.c: The Father is whom Philip wants to see; the time comes before that.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-02.hint: Look for an expression of time.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-03.question: How does Thomas's question in John 14:5 prepare Jesus' answer?
joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-03.feedbackCorrect: Thomas's doubt opens the way for Jesus to declare himself the way.

feedbackWrong.b: Thomas admits he does not know; he has not understood yet.
feedbackWrong.c: The question does not end things; it receives Jesus' great answer.
feedbackWrong.d: The subject is still the way to the Father.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-03.hint: See what Jesus declares right after.

options.a: It opens the way for Jesus to reveal himself
options.b: It proves Thomas already understood
options.c: It ends the disciples' conversation
options.d: It changes the subject to the temple

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-04.question: How does the conversation in John 14:5–6 move forward?
joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-04.feedbackCorrect: From Thomas's doubt to Jesus' claim to be the only way to the Father.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with Thomas's question; reaching the Father closes the answer.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-04.hint: The question comes before the declaration.

options.a: Thomas admits not knowing the way
options.b: Jesus declares himself way, truth and life
options.c: Only through Jesus does one reach the Father

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-05.question: In John 14:5, where does Thomas say he doesn't know Jesus is going?
joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-05.feedbackCorrect: Thomas does not know where Jesus is going, so he asks.

feedbackWrong.a: Thomas's doubt is about Jesus' destination, not his words.
feedbackWrong.c: Thomas speaks of Jesus going, not of a return at that moment.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-05.hint: Read the verb in Thomas's question.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-06.question: What links John 14:6 to Exodus 3:14?
joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus' "Eu sou" echoes the name by which God revealed himself to Moses.

feedbackWrong.b: In both texts, the one presenting himself is God himself.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus does not deny God; he presents himself in God's words.

joao-cam-jo-02-eu-sou-06.hint: Compare how God and Jesus present themselves.

options.a: God reveals himself as I Am
options.b: A human name for God
options.c: Jesus denies the God of old

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-01.question: In John 14:9, whoever sees Jesus also sees the Father.
joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus answers Philip that whoever sees him is already seeing the Father.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 14:9: "Quem me vê vê o Pai", Jesus says.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-02.question: In John 14:6, tap the phrase showing the way to the Father goes through Jesus.
joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus states that no one comes to the Father except through him.

feedbackWrong.a: "vida" says who Jesus is; the way to the Father comes at the end.
feedbackWrong.b: "verdade" says who Jesus is; the way to the Father comes at the end.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-02.hint: Read the end of the verse.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-03.question: What reading does John 14:6 support about coming to the Father?
joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus presents himself as the way, and no one goes to the Father without him.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus says no one comes to the Father except through him.
feedbackWrong.c: Thomas has just said he does not know the way.
feedbackWrong.d: The text points to a person, Jesus, not just ideas.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-03.hint: See the final sentence of John 14:6.

options.a: There are ways to the Father without Jesus
options.b: Jesus is the only way to the Father
options.c: Thomas already knew the whole way
options.d: Knowing ideas about God is enough

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-04.question: Which sequence reveals the thread of "I Am" in the Bible's story?
joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-04.feedbackCorrect: From God's name in Exodus to Jesus' claim and to faith in him.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story, from Exodus to the Gospel of John.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-04.hint: Start with God revealing himself to Moses.

options.a: God presents himself as I Am
options.b: Jesus says he is the way to the Father
options.c: Whoever believes reaches the Father in him

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-05.question: In John 14:9, what verb does Jesus repeat when speaking of seeing the Father?
joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-05.feedbackCorrect: Whoever sees Jesus sees the Father, for he reveals God to the disciples.

feedbackWrong.a: Knowing appears in the verse, but the repeated verb is another.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of hearing here, but of seeing Jesus.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-05.hint: It is the verb tied to Jesus and the Father.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-06.question: What links John 14:9 to John 1:18?
joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-06.feedbackCorrect: No one has seen God, but Jesus reveals him; so seeing Jesus is seeing the Father.

feedbackWrong.a: It is precisely in Jesus that Philip sees the Father, in 14:9.
feedbackWrong.c: John 1:18 says no one has ever seen God directly.

joao-pro-jo-02-eu-sou-06.hint: See who, according to John, reveals God.

options.a: Philip did not need Jesus
options.b: Jesus reveals the invisible Father
options.c: The Father can be seen on his own

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.question: In John 15:5, Jesus says he is the vine and the disciples are the branches.
joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus presents himself as the vine, and the disciples as the branches.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 15:5: "Eu sou a videira, vocês são os ramos".

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.hint: Read the first sentence of the verse.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.question: In John 15:5, tap who the disciples are in Jesus' image.
joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: The disciples are the branches joined to Jesus, the vine.

feedbackWrong.a: "fruto" is the result of the branches, not who they are.
feedbackWrong.b: "videira" is Jesus; the disciples have another role in the image.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.hint: See what Jesus says after "vocês são".

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.question: According to John 15:2, what happens to the branch that bears no fruit?
joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: The branch that is in Jesus and bears no fruit is cut off.

feedbackWrong.b: Pruning is for those who bear fruit, so they bear more.
feedbackWrong.c: Without fruit, the branch is cut off; it does not produce alone.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not speak of replanting, but of cutting off.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.hint: Read the first part of the verse.

options.a: It is cut off
options.b: It is left unpruned
options.c: It produces more on its own

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.question: Arrange John 15:5 in the order of the text.
joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: Jesus is the vine, and whoever remains in him bears much fruit.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with Jesus and the branches; the fruit closes the verse.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.hint: The verse begins with the vine.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.question: In John 15:4, what must the branch remain in to bear fruit?
joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: The branch bears fruit only if it remains in the vine, which is Jesus.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus' image is a plant, not a spring of water.
feedbackWrong.c: The image is of the vine and branches, not of a house.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.hint: Think of the plant in Jesus' image.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-06.question: What does John 15:5 convey that connects to this context?
joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: Joined to Jesus as a branch to the vine, the disciple bears much fruit.

feedbackWrong.b: Fruit comes from remaining in Jesus, in John 15:4–5.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus says that without him we can do nothing.

joao-sem-jo-03-adeus-espirito-06.hint: See where the branch gets its life.

options.a: Joined to Jesus, we bear fruit
options.b: Fruit without remaining in Jesus
options.c: On our own, we produce everything

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.question: In John 15:4, the branch bears fruit only if it remains in the vine.
joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: By itself the branch bears no fruit; it must remain in the vine.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 15:4: the branch cannot bear fruit by itself.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.hint: See the condition Jesus sets out.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.question: In John 15:2, tap the phrase that shows the purpose of pruning the branch.
joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: The branch is pruned for a purpose: to bear even more fruit.

feedbackWrong.a: "limpa" is the action done; the purpose comes right after.
feedbackWrong.c: "frutos" is the result sought; the purpose comes just before.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.hint: Look for two little words before "produza".

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.question: How does John 15:2 relate to John 15:5?
joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: Pruning prepares the branch that remains in Jesus for more fruit.

feedbackWrong.b: Pruning does not replace remaining; it prepares for fruit.
feedbackWrong.c: The fruitful branch is precisely the one pruned, in 15:2.
feedbackWrong.d: Cut-off branches are fruitless; pruned ones bear more.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.hint: See why the branch is pruned.

options.a: Pruning prepares branches to bear fruit
options.b: Pruning replaces remaining in Jesus
options.c: Bearing fruit needs no pruning at all

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.question: How does the teaching in John 15:4–5 move forward?
joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: From the call to remain to the promise of much fruit in Jesus.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the call to remain; fruit is the final result.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.hint: The result comes at the end of verse 5.

options.a: The branch must remain in the vine
options.b: Jesus presents himself as the vine
options.c: Whoever remains bears much fruit

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.question: In John 15:8, what happens to the Father when the disciples bear much fruit?
joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.feedbackCorrect: When the disciples bear much fruit, the Father is glorified in it.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of calling the Father, but of glorifying him.
feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of the Father receiving glory from the disciples' fruit.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.hint: See what the fruit brings about for the Father.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-06.question: What links John 15:5 to Galatians 5:22?
joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-06.feedbackCorrect: In John fruit comes from remaining in Jesus; in Paul, from the Spirit.

feedbackWrong.a: The fruit of the Spirit goes together with remaining in Jesus.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus says that without him the branch can do nothing.

joao-cam-jo-03-adeus-espirito-06.hint: Compare where fruit comes from in both texts.

options.a: The Spirit makes Jesus Christ unnecessary
options.b: Fruit comes from isolated effort
options.c: Fruit grows from a connected life

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.question: In John 15:5, the disciples can produce everything without Jesus.
joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus says the opposite: without him the disciples can do nothing.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of John 15:5: "sem mim nada podem fazer".

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-01.hint: Read the last words of the verse.

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.question: In John 15:5, tap the phrase that shows the disciples' dependence.
joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.feedbackCorrect: Without Jesus they can do nothing; all the branch's life comes from him.

feedbackWrong.a: Much fruit is the result; the dependence appears at the end.
feedbackWrong.c: The branches are the disciples; the dependence comes later.

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-02.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.question: What reading does John 15:4–5 support about the disciple's life?
joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.feedbackCorrect: Without remaining in Jesus there is no fruit; life depends on him.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus calls us to remain continually, not briefly.
feedbackWrong.c: In 15:7, Jesus' words also remain in the disciples.
feedbackWrong.d: The branch is not self-sufficient; by itself it bears no fruit.

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-03.hint: See what happens without remaining in him.

options.a: A brief first contact is enough
options.b: A fruitful life depends on Jesus
options.c: Remaining does not require his words
options.d: Fruit proves the branch is self-sufficient

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of John 15:5?
joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.feedbackCorrect: Remaining in Jesus sustains the branch, and the fruit glorifies the Father.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with remaining; glorifying the Father is where it ends.

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-04.hint: Go from branch to fruit, and from fruit to the Father.

options.a: The branch remains in Jesus
options.b: Jesus' life sustains the branch
options.c: The fruit glorifies the Father

joao-pro-jo-03-adeus-espirito-05.question: In John 15:7, what of Jesus must remain in the disciples?
